title: News Conditions

launchpad.outcome: See how a scheduled release changes the environment, and apply the news rule you already built.
launchpad.missionQuestion: What does my saved news rule say right now?

slides.title: Watch the environment change
slides.example: No new entries within 5 minutes before selected high-impact events.

asks.prompt: Did the setup exist in the same environment for the entire sequence?

options.label: Yes, it’s the same chart
options.feedback: Same chart. Different conditions minute to minute.

options.label: No
options.why: THE SETUP DIDN’T EXIST IN THE SAME ENVIRONMENT FOR THE ENTIRE SEQUENCE.

lines: But news does NOT automatically invalidate every setup.

slides.title: Valid ICC. Event in 4 minutes.
slides.punch: Your saved rule. Not re-written, not re-negotiated. Just read.

slides.title: Where does the event time come from?

asks.prompt: Tomorrow there’s a scheduled release. How do you know?

options.label: The Academy tells me in the simulator
options.feedback: Simulator events are practice. The Academy never invents real news events.

options.label: I check a real economic calendar before my session
options.why: Then your news rule already knows what to do.

options.label: I’ll notice when the candle gets big
options.feedback: That’s the surprise this lesson exists to prevent.

slides.quote: The calendar is public. Read it before the bell, not after the candle.

slides.prompt: How does a scheduled event change your environment, and what decides your response?
slides.modelAnswer: It can change volatility, liquidity, fills and candle size around the release. It doesn’t automatically invalidate a setup. My saved news rule decides, and I check the calendar before the session.

remember: A SCHEDULED EVENT SHOULDN’T SURPRISE YOU JUST BECAUSE THE CANDLE DID.
